topic.title_he: יום הולדת שלא הולך לפי התוכנית
topic.reason: הנושא נקבע לפי התוכנית השבועית (אצווה 2026-10-25, משבצת 2 מתוך 7): כל חבילה על נושא אחר. יום הולדת שנגמר בבכי (בשיר, מול הנרות, או בערב שאחרי) קורה בכל חודש בשנה, ולכן אין כאן טענה על לוח שנה. בקטלוג יש ספר שמתאים להמשך בהודעה הפרטית (יום הולדת, ספר 15, גילאי 3 עד 8), ולכן סיפור אישי בשקופית האחרונה הוא המשך טבעי. רגיש: לא להציג את ההורה כמי שקלקל את המסיבה, ולא לדבר על סוכר או על התנהגות רעה.

voice.note: קול מכויל: 37 דוגמאות מהעריכות של ירין. הכתיבה לפי השינויים האחרונים שלו: סיכום בלי רשימה, דיבור על הילדים ברבים בשקופיות המקצועיות, דוגמה אחת ברורה בכל שורת כותרת.

sources.title: Helping Toddlers Develop Self-Control From 24-36 Months
sources.publisher: ZERO TO THREE (19 May 2025)
sources.quote: Use what you know about your child to plan ahead. ... you may want to start flipping through the family photo album in the weeks before you attend a big family picnic ... you might give him a warning 5 minutes beforehand ... Choices help children feel in control. ... Tantrums mean your child is overwhelmed and needs your help to regain control.
sources.supports: Plan ahead and preview a big event; a 5 minute warning before a change; choices help children feel in control; a meltdown means the child is overwhelmed and needs an adult's help. Written for 24 to 36 months; applied to age 4 as an analogy.

sources.title: Keeping Birthday Stress to a Minimum
sources.publisher: PBS KIDS for Parents (24 Jul 2017)
sources.quote: If appropriate, consider partnering with or even handing off some of the planning responsibilities to your child, or partnering with them for the planning. Frank insists, "They can pick their favorite theme, games, friends and food."
sources.supports: Letting the child pick parts of the party (theme, games, food).

sources.title: Age-by-Age Birthday Party Guide
sources.publisher: PBS KIDS for Parents (1 May 2024)
sources.quote: It's best to put away your child's favorite toys before inviting a party full of friends over (sharing and taking turns will come later).
sources.supports: Putting the birthday child's favourite toys away before friends arrive. Written in the age 2 section; applied to age 4 as an analogy, in the child's imagined voice.

sources.title: Temper Tantrums
sources.publisher: Nemours KidsHealth (reviewed June 2022, Elizabeth M. Schilling, PhD)
sources.quote: Tantrums may happen when kids are tired, hungry, or uncomfortable. ... If your child is tired or hungry, it's time for a nap or a snack.
sources.supports: Tired or hungry children are more likely to melt down; food before the party.

sources.title: How to Help Kids Cope With Disappointment
sources.publisher: PBS KIDS for Parents, Katie Hurley, LCSW (16 Jan 2019)
sources.quote: the word “might” is very important. Young children have a tendency to engage in all-or-nothing thinking. ... Make a list to indicate hopes, possibilities and sure things. ... Use empathic responses like, “I understand that this is difficult. I know you feel disappointed right now.” Give your child the time and space to cry, feel sad and soak up a hug from mom or dad. Connection helps kids recover from adversity. Meet heated responses with calm ones to model healthy coping strategies and save the discussion for a later, calmer moment. ... Read or ask a parent to read to you
sources.supports: Managing anticipation with hopes, possibilities and sure things; empathy and a hug first, the talk later; reading together is one of the calming ideas listed.

sources.title: Temper Tantrums
sources.publisher: Nemours KidsHealth (reviewed June 2022, Elizabeth M. Schilling, PhD)
sources.quote: Tantrums may happen when kids are tired, hungry, or uncomfortable. ... Know your child's limits. If you know your toddler is tired, it's not the best time to go grocery shopping or try to squeeze in one more errand. ... Remind yourself that your job is helping your child learn to calm down. So you need to be calm too. ... If your child is tired or hungry, it's time for a nap or a snack.
sources.supports: Tiredness and hunger make meltdowns more likely; no extra outing when tired; the parent's calm helps the child calm down; rest or a snack.

sources.title: Age-by-Age Birthday Party Guide
sources.publisher: PBS KIDS for Parents (1 May 2024)
sources.quote: Keep the party to about 90 minutes to avoid over-stimulating them (and exhausting you).
sources.supports: A birthday party can over-stimulate young children (age 3 section, applied to age 5 as an analogy).

sources.title: How to Help Kids Cope With Disappointment
sources.publisher: PBS KIDS for Parents, Katie Hurley, LCSW (16 Jan 2019)
sources.quote: Remember that your child is coming to you because she needs empathy and understanding, not a rock-solid coping plan. ... save the discussion for a later, calmer moment. ... Listen to soft music Read or ask a parent to read to you Get outside to play Snuggle up with a stuffed animal and a few favorite toys ... Be patient when your child has big reactions to seemingly small events.
sources.supports: Empathy rather than questioning in the moment; soft music, a stuffed animal and reading together as calming ideas; patience with big reactions to small things.

sources.title: Playful Birthday Party Ideas & Tips for Young Children
sources.publisher: American Academy of Pediatrics, HealthyChildren.org (last updated 31 Aug 2022, adapted from Melissa & Doug)
sources.quote: The rule of thumb for babies and toddlers is your child's age, plus one. So, if your kiddo is turning 3, four attendees is a good number of kid guests. If they're turning 4, try to keep the guest list to five kids. Remember, big crowds can overwhelm young kids ... Keep the party under 90 minutes for toddlers; school-aged kids can last about 2-3 hours. And be mindful of naptime if your child is at that stage. Structured but flexible Plan for around 10-15 minutes for each game or activity to keep kids engaged, but if the kiddos are really enjoying something in particular, let 'em play!
sources.supports: Guests: age plus one (five for a child turning 4); big crowds can overwhelm young kids; short parties; mind naptime; 10 to 15 minutes per activity, longer if they enjoy it.

sources.title: Age-by-Age Birthday Party Guide
sources.publisher: PBS KIDS for Parents (1 May 2024)
sources.quote: It's best not to open gifts at the party since most guests won't understand that they can't take theirs home. ... Keep the party to about 90 minutes to avoid over-stimulating them (and exhausting you). ... Plan short games and keep things moving because fours may find it hard to wait their turn. ... Plan for a party of about two hours.
sources.supports: Open presents after the party (age 2 and age 3 sections); about 90 minutes at 3 and about two hours at 4; short games because fours find it hard to wait their turn.

sources.title: How to Help Kids Cope With Disappointment
sources.publisher: PBS KIDS for Parents, Katie Hurley, LCSW (16 Jan 2019)
sources.quote: It’s natural to build excitement for something like a family trip by talking about all of the wonderful things that might happen, but the word “might” is very important. Young children have a tendency to engage in all-or-nothing thinking. ... Make a list to indicate hopes, possibilities and sure things. ... Use empathic responses like, “I understand that this is difficult. I know you feel disappointed right now.” Give your child the time and space to cry, feel sad and soak up a hug from mom or dad. Connection helps kids recover from adversity. Meet heated responses with calm ones to model healthy coping strategies and save the discussion for a later, calmer moment. ... It’s important to act as a guide when it comes to managing setbacks instead of jumping in with the fix. ... How did it feel when that happened? What did you wish would happen? What can be done differently the next time? ... Read or ask a parent to read to you
sources.supports: All or nothing thinking in young children; managing anticipation with hopes, possibilities and sure things; empathy, time to cry and a hug; meeting heat with calm; guide rather than fix; the talk later with questions; reading together as a calming idea.

sources.title: Age-by-Age Birthday Party Guide
sources.publisher: PBS KIDS for Parents (1 May 2024)
sources.quote: Five-year-olds know parties are very important and may enjoy the planning even more than the event itself. That's why it's especially important to involve your five-year-old in the entire process.
sources.supports: Involving a five year old in planning the party.

sources.title: Temper Tantrums
sources.publisher: Nemours KidsHealth (reviewed June 2022, Elizabeth M. Schilling, PhD)
sources.quote: Remind yourself that your job is helping your child learn to calm down. So you need to be calm too.
sources.supports: The parent's calm helps the child calm down.

sources.title: How to Help Your Kids Handle Disappointment
sources.publisher: Child Mind Institute, Christina Frank (reviewed 6 Nov 2023)
sources.quote: What you can do is listen to and acknowledge children’s frustration and disappointment ... As parents, our first impulse is often to try to fix problems for our children. ... It’s also important to avoid judging their reactions.
sources.supports: Acknowledge the disappointment instead of rushing to fix it. Written about cancelled events (including birthdays) during the pandemic; applied here to a birthday that goes differently.
